title: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets
summary: A ground study that re-analysed more than 1,600 camera images from the SPICE space-station flames to measure soot and temperature. It asked why flames make so much more soot in microgravity than on Earth.
objective: This ground investigation  sought to increase understanding of the issues that control the large discrepancy between soot formation in 1g and in 0g flames.
varied: Normal gravity versus microgravity, and soot-model settings (radiation, scattering, boundary conditions, heat transfer to the burner).

title: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling using Flamelet Generated Manifolds in Microgravity with Comparison to BASS Experiments using Two-Color Tomography
summary: A ground modelling study that built a new computer model of flames spreading along solid materials in microgravity. It checked the model against camera images from the BASS and BASS-II space-station burns.
objective: The objective of this research was to develop and validate new flamelet generated manifold (FGM) modeling techniques for concurrent flame spread in microgravity.

fuel.detail: flat sheets, spheres, and rod-shaped polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) samples, as well as wax cylinders

title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II
summary: Saffire-II burned nine different spacecraft materials inside an empty Cygnus cargo ship after it left the space station, to compare how each burns in low gravity against NASA's Earth screening test.
objective: The objectives of SAFFIRE-II are to determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity and to investigate the low-g flammability limits compared to those obtained in NASA’s normal gravity material flammability screening test.

fuel.detail: SIBAL, silicone, structure PMMA, flat PMMA, and PMMA with Nomex

conditions.airflow: air flow velocity of either 20 or 30 cm/s

varied: Sample material, airflow speed (20 or 30 cm/s) and airflow direction.
publications: Buoyant Effects on the Flammability of Silicone Samples Planned for the Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire), Conference: 45th International Conference on Environmental Systems ICES-2015-[293] 12-16 July 2015, Bellevue, Washington

title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-III
summary: Saffire-III repeated the large-fabric burn inside an empty Cygnus cargo ship after it left the space station, this time with faster airflow and the air blowing with or against the flame.
objective: determine how rapidly a large scale fire grows in low-gravity
varied: Airflow direction: with the flame (concurrent) or against it (opposed).
publications: Buoyant Effects on the Flammability of Silicone Samples Planned for the Spacecraft Fire Experiment (Saffire), 45th International Conference on Environmental Systems ICES-2015-[293] 12-16 July 2015, Bellevue, Washington

title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-Reflight
summary: SAME-R reflew the SAME smoke experiment on the space station with a new foam material, hotter heating and a new instrument, after contamination spoiled samples from the first flight. It completed 66 test points.
objective: the primary objective of the SAME-R investigation was to quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity

fuel.detail: Pyrell®, an intumescent fire-retardant foam by Foamex

varied: Test material, heating temperature, and whether air flowed during heating, across 66 test points.
publications: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment-2: Comparison of Flight Experiment Results with Ground Test Results

title: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
summary: SAME heated spacecraft materials until they smoked, aboard the space station, and measured the smoke particles. The worry it tested: smoke particles may grow bigger without gravity, and some detectors might then fail to alarm.
objective: One of the major goals of this investigation was to quantify the sizes that the liquid smoke particulate achieves in low gravity
varied: Sample temperature, flow field and particle aging time.

title: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
summary: SLICE lit small gas flames on burner tubes aboard the space station to see how they hold on to the burner, lift off, and make soot without gravity. More than 4,000 photos were taken across 13 tests.
objective: The objective of this investigation is to better understand the structure and stability of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity.
varied: Fuel, burner diameter, coflow air speed and nitrogen dilution.

hardware.apparatus: fan-driven flow duct, exchangeable burner tubes, and integrated sensors

publications: A computational and experimental study of coflow laminar methane/air diffusion flames: Effects of fuel dilution, inlet velocity, and gravity

title: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
summary: SPICE lit 526 small gas-jet flames in the space station's glovebox and turned up the fuel until each one began to give off soot, its 'smoke point'. It compared fuels, burner sizes and air speeds.
objective: Identify the laminar smoke-point properties of non-buoyant jet diffusion flames under various co-flow conditions in microgravity.

fuel.detail: methane, ethylene, propane, propylene, and propylene mixtures

conditions.airflow: co-flow velocities ranging from 5.4 cm/s to 65 cm/s

varied: Fuel, burner diameter (0.41, 0.76 or 1.6 mm), co-flow air speed and fuel flow rate.

hardware.apparatus: a flow duct with integrated nozzles, cameras, and fuel delivery systems

publications: Laminar Smoke Points in Coflow Measured Aboard the International Space Station

title: Utilization of the Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment Data for Advanced Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Micro-Gravity
summary: A ground computer-simulation study, built on the SAME space-station smoke experiment, of how gravity changes the size of smoke particles coming off a heated material. Smoke particle size matters because it decides whether a detector notices it.
objective: The objective of this investigation was to use numerical simulation to explore the influence of gravity on pyrolysis smoke growth from a fundamental perspective.
varied: Earth gravity versus microgravity, and two low cross-flow speeds.

title: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: A Multidimensional Multi-Physics CFD Analysis
summary: A ground computer-modelling study, checked against FLEX space-station data, of how small pushes of heat or airflow decide whether a droplet's cool flame keeps burning, flares into a hot flame, or goes out.
objective: The objective of this ground investigation was to use flight data obtained from PSI through NASA’s Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX) to quantify how externally imposed thermal and convective perturbations regulated the dynamics and ultimate fate of already established droplet cool flames

fuel.size: large (1–4 mm) and sub-millimeter (~0.5 mm) droplets

varied: Imposed airflow, imposed heating, or both; how strong and how fast the forcing was; the surrounding gas mix; and pressure.
publications: Extinction characteristics of isolated n-alkane fuel droplets during low temperature cool flame burning in air (2023)

title: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation / Stretch Extinction Using Counterflow Flames
summary: A ground study that used FLEX space-station data to work out when a hot flame turns into a low-temperature 'cool flame' and when that cool flame goes out. It combined computer simulations with counterflow flame experiments on Earth.
objective: Develop a new diagram of the flammability limits of diffusional cool flames affected by radiation, diffusion, and convection.
varied: Oxygen concentration, dilution and pressure, in simulations of cool-flame extinction.

title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
summary: ACME CFI-G fed gas through a small spherical burner aboard the space station to create steady cool flames from gaseous fuels for the first time, and to see what makes them go out or turn into hot flames.
objective: Determine the conditions for which cool diffusion flames occur for propane, n-butane, and n-pentane
varied: Fuel, dilution, flow rate, pressure and flow direction (normal or inverse flames).
publications: Spherical gas-fueled cool diffusion flames
